definition: Governing how long a model thinks, and across 4 sources a control problem with one well-documented trap. The trap: a length incentive not gated on the answer being correct is satisfied vacuously -- an unconstrained reward exploited to the context limit, a target-constrained penalty buying coherent but functionally useless filler at essentially collapsed accuracy, and only a bonus conditional on correctness converting preserved length into accuracy. The archive's related structural finding is that control is concentrated in a single special token rather than distributed over the trace, which is why cue-appending works and also why it is a property of a model that has learned to treat that token as a cue. Two design points from the corpus: a uniform token limit is wrong for every query whose solution length differs from the average, which is why per-query limits derived from that query's own thinking responses beat it; and token-level decoupling lets the budget be spent unevenly within a response.

evidence.note: Shows on four internal Netflix verification tasks that explicit reasoning usually degrades subjective judgement, that applying RLVR to fix it makes the policy abandon deliberation for short heuristic guessing, and that a length bonus gated on answer correctness is what stops the collapse.
evidence.title: LLM Reasoning for Subjective Tasks: Failure Modes, Mitigation, and Dynamic Reasoning Routing

evidence.note: Defines a token's marginal utility as its log-probability gain for the ground-truth answer, then trains against negative-utility tokens to shorten chains of thought.
evidence.title: Think Better, Not Longer: Token-Level Marginal Utility for Efficient Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Fixes reward hacking in hybrid thinking/non-thinking RL by setting per-query token limits for non-thinking responses derived from the solution part of that query's thinking responses.
evidence.title: Thinking-Based Non-Thinking: Solving the Reward Hacking Problem in Training Hybrid Reasoning Models via Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Attributes efficiency-training damage to sequence-level coupling between efficiency and correctness rewards, and decouples them by applying the efficiency reward only to a single mode-selection token.
evidence.title: ADaPT: Token-Level Decoupling for Efficient Large Reasoning Models

name: length control
